nodes.text: Let $k\geq 3$. Does there exist some $f(k)$ such that if a graph $G$ has chromatic number $\geq f(k)$ then $G$ must contain some odd cycle whose vertices span a graph of chromatic number $\geq k$?

#640 : [Er97d,p.84] graph theory | chromatic number A problem of Erdős and Hajnal. This is trivial when $k=3$, since any non-bipartite graph contains an odd cycle, and all odd cycles have chromatic number $3$. Steiner has observed in the comments that this is equivalent to the problem in which we replace 'odd cycle' with 'path'.
